description: This course provides modelling of various power system components and covers load flow analysis, fault analysis and stability analysis of a power system network, along with computer methods for power system studies.

syllabus.title: Introduction
syllabus.body: Review of per unit system. Modeling of power system components, single line impedance and reactance diagram, incidence matrices using graph theory, bus admittance and impedance matrix using graph theory. Y-bus formulation with phase shifter and transformers.

syllabus.title: Load Flow Analysis
syllabus.body: Introduction, bus classification, nodal admittance matrix, Gauss-Seidel method, Newton-Raphson method, fast decoupled method, algorithms, flow charts, merits and demerits of the above methods.

syllabus.title: Fault Analysis
syllabus.body: Symmetrical fault analysis: transient on a transmission line, three-phase short-circuit on a synchronous machine, algorithm for Z-bus formulation, analysis through impedance matrix, current limiting reactors. Symmetrical components: symmetrical components transformation, sequence impedance and sequence networks of power system components. Unsymmetrical fault analysis: LG, LL, LLG using transformation matrix method, analysis through impedance matrix.

syllabus.title: Stability Analysis and Computer Methods in Power Systems
syllabus.body: Power system stability: steady-state, transient and dynamic stability, rotor dynamics and the swing equation, equal area criterion and its applications, step-by-step solution of swing equation, factors affecting transient stability, methods to improve steady state and transient stability, introduction to voltage stability. Computer methods in power systems: simulation of various load flow methods, simulation of various faults in a power system network, transient stability algorithm using modified Euler's method and fourth order Runge-Kutta method.

outcomes: Understand the graph theory approach for formulation of Y-bus and Z-bus and application of the p.u. system.
Apply Gauss-Seidel and Newton-Raphson techniques for load flow analysis.
Analyze symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults using symmetrical component theory.
Investigate the stability of a power system under small-signal and large-signal disturbances.
textbooks: J. J. Grainger and W. D. Stevenson, Power System Analysis, McGraw Hill Education, 1st Edition, 2003.
D. P. Kothari and I. J. Nagrath, Modern Power System Analysis, Tata McGraw Hill Education, 4th Edition, 2011.
H. Saadat, Power System Analysis, Tata McGraw Hill Education, 2nd Edition, 2002.
referenceBooks: G. W. Stagg and A. H. El-Abiad, Computer Methods in Power System Analysis, McGraw Hill ISE, 1986.
